title: Input.valueAsNumber can not be manually set to NaN despite it being a valid value for it
body:
Per the specification, `NaN` is a valid value for the `valueAsNumber` property of a Input Element.
It gets set to `NaN` when `value` is `''` for example (making it the default value).

However, the setter for `valueAsNumber` is [defined thusly](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-valueasnumber):

> On setting, if the new value is infinite, then throw a [TypeError](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception. Otherwise, if the [valueAsNumber](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-valueasnumber) attribute [does not apply](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#do-not-apply), as defined for the [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#the-input-element) element's [type](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-type) attribute's current state, then throw an ["InvalidStateError"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [DOMException](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). Otherwise, if the new value is a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then set the [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-value) of the element to the empty string. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a number to a string](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#concept-input-value-number-string), as defined for that state, on the new value, and set the [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-value) of the element to the resulting string.

Where particular importance in this case is on the first line, which excludes all infinite values. `NaN` as it happens, ~is considered an infinite value~, seems to be considered an infinite value by some browsers, so they never get to the case further down the paragraph that explicitly handles `NaN`, as we have already errored out, per the first line.

- Safari follows this logic "correctly", erroring out. So does the JSDOM project, used in Jest.
- Firefox does the sensible (but seemingly incompliant) thing of accepting `NaN` without any complaint and setting `value` to `''`
- Chrome and its derivatives also (seemingly) incompliantly accept `NaN` and set `value` to `''` but throw a warning that the value could not be parsed (despite it actually being parsed just fine)

It would seem reasonable to allow the manual setting of `valueAsNumber` to `NaN` as the Spec is already having an explicit instruction as to how to handle that exact situation, but due to ordering leaves a confusing (and seemingly) unreachable condition.

A simple fix would be to move the conditional for `NaN` to the top of the specification, thus resolving the confusing condition without impacting the rest, and hopefully getting browsers to unify their behaviour on this issue.

Edit: Updated the statement about NaN being considered infinite to not sound so authoritative, slightly reworded parts about compliance in the same direction.
